blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Mary Kom, though not covered in the earlier thematic chapters, is one of Manipur's most nationally and internationally recognised individuals and a frequently tested 'notable person from Manipur' fact in general-knowledge exams — an Olympic bronze medallist (2012 London) and multiple-time World Amateur Boxing Champion.

items: Manipur: approx 22,327 sq km; borders Nagaland, Mizoram, Assam, and Myanmar; capital: Imphal.
Imphal Valley = ~10% of area but majority of population (Meitei); surrounding hills = ~90% of area (Naga, Kuki-Zo).
Loktak Lake = largest freshwater lake in North-East India; Keibul Lamjao National Park = world's only floating national park.
Cheitharol Kumbaba traces the Ningthouja dynasty from 33 CE; Garibniwaz converted the Meitei to Vaishnavite Hinduism (1709-48).
'Seven Years' Devastation' (1819-26, Burmese occupation) ended by the Treaty of Yandabo (1826).
Anglo-Manipur War (1891): Tikendrajit Singh & Thangal General hanged 13 August 1891 — Patriots' Day.
Battle of Imphal (1944) halted the Japanese WWII invasion of India; Moirang = INA flag-hoisting site (1944).
Manipur State Constitution Act (1947) + elected State Assembly (1948) — before merger with India (Sept 1949).
UT status 1956-1972; full statehood 21 January 1972, with Meghalaya and Tripura.
60-seat Assembly: 20 ST-reserved, 0 SC-reserved. Current CM: Yumnam Khemchand Singh (since 4 Feb 2026); Governor: Ajay Kumar Bhalla (since 3 Jan 2025).
President's Rule: 13 Feb 2025 - 4 Feb 2026 (Assembly kept in suspended animation, not dissolved).
Rice dominates valley agriculture; Chak-hao (black rice) is a distinctive GI product; Moreh is a key India-Myanmar border-trade town.
Population (2011) approx 28.56 lakh; ST share approx 40%; Meitei (valley, Hindu/Sanamahi) vs Naga & Kuki-Zo (hills, Christian, ST).
Manipuri dance = 1 of India's 8 classical dance forms (Raas Leela); Sagol Kangjei = origin of modern polo.
Sangai deer ('Dancing Deer') = state animal, found only at Keibul Lamjao National Park; Shirui Lily = endemic to Ukhrul district.
Ethnic violence began May 2023 (Meitei-Kuki-Zo); over 250 reported deaths, large-scale displacement; situation remained evolving as of 2026.
